title: The Best Protocol For Quitting P*rn
author: Ad Aeternum
summary: The author of Ad Aeternum offers a seven-step Christian protocol for young men who want to quit pornography, framing quitting as a modern rite of passage into mature manhood built on self-control. The steps are to see the habit for what it is, remove digital and physical triggers, create incentives and penalties, separate identity from the habit by dropping streak counting, rely on God and prayer, fast and confess frequently, and stay busy and relentless. He argues that negative reinforcement works better than positive for this vice and that counting days gives the habit too much importance. The tone is strongly moral and explicitly Catholic in places, relying on prayer, the sacrament of confession and Marian devotion, with a note that non-Catholics can still try confession. He closes by inviting readers to share advice in the comments as a collective forum.
points: The author treats quitting pornography as a rite of passage for young men, tying male maturity to self-control over lower impulses.
He recommends removing triggers aggressively in both the digital and physical environment, including unfollowing provocative accounts and discarding triggering media.
He argues against counting porn-free days, because tracking a streak makes the habit more important and makes a relapse feel like starting over.
Incentives should be mostly negative, with an uncomfortable consequence such as cold showers or fasting after a relapse.
The spiritual core is prayer, fasting and frequent confession, with the claim that naming sin aloud is a humbling practice hard to replicate outside confession.
quotes: I see quitting p0rn as the new “rite of passage” that young men need to go through to leave childhood behind and mature into the men they could be.
A man who’s still controlled by his impulses and lower faculties is a man who hasn’t yet fully developed, and thus behaves like a boy.
The goal in this first step is to make it impossible for you to hide behind ignorance —willful or otherwise—, and make it impossible for you to justify any usage of p0rn.
Unfollow even female “friends” who post provocative content. This might sound extreme, and it is. But it’s your soul that’s at stake.
Everything around you can either aid you in your pursuit of virtue, or hinder you.
I believe for quitting p0rnography, negative reinforcement is much more powerful than positive reinforcement.

Keeping count of something makes it important. It keeps it relevant. If you are constantly keeping count of the days you've been porn-free, you are telling your brain that this is massively important and extremely difficult.

Fasting is one of the most effective ways to control lust because by controlling the appetite for food, you also learn the self-control necessary to keep other bodily appetites —such as sexual desire— at bay.
